extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media scholars, and general readers interested in media ethics and news-reporting standards
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria for news organizations when reporting on documentary evidence (memos, records): authentication, provenance/chain-of-custody, expert use, corroboration, vetting, conflict-of-interest avoidance, and accurate representation of sources and experts. Derived from the Killian documents controversy and the Thornburgh–Boccardi panel findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain clear authentication of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure to obtain clear authentication of any of the Killian documents was identified as a most serious defect in the reporting and production of the segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations must secure clear, professional authentication of documentary evidence before relying on them in a report. Authentication from qualified document examiners is required; using only faxed or photocopied duplicates can make professional authentication impossible. Do not air claims based on documents unless authenticity can be established to professional standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurately represent what experts actually said
rubrics_metrics.description: The segment contained the false statement that an expert had authenticated the Killian documents when all he had done was authenticate one signature from one document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise in attributing expert opinions—do not overstate or generalize limited findings (e.g., signature match vs full-document authentication). Disclose limits and uncertainties of expert conclusions; avoid wording that implies broader endorsement than given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize the background and credibility of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel found a failure to scrutinize the publicly available, and at times controversial, background of the source of the documents, retired Lieutenant Colonel Bill Burkett.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and disclose source background, incentives, prior statements, and credibility issues. Background checks and documentation of source reliability are necessary, especially for sensitive allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and document chain of custody/provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: There was a failure to find and interview the individual who was understood to be Burkett's source of the Killian documents, and thus to establish the chain of custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace and document the provenance of physical or documentary evidence; identify intermediaries and original holders. Where chain-of-custody cannot be established, treat the material with caution and disclose the limitation to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a factual basis for claims of origin/provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure to establish a basis for the statement in the segment that the documents 'were taken from Colonel Killian's personal files' was criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assert provenance (e.g., 'from X's personal files') unless you have verifiable evidence. If provenance is asserted by a source, seek independent corroboration before presenting it as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop adequate corroboration with official records
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel criticized the failure to develop adequate corroboration to support the statements in the Killian documents and to carefully compare the Killian documents to official TexANG records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check documentary claims against official records, personnel files, dates, and other contemporaneous materials. Corroboration can reveal inconsistencies (e.g., personnel discharge dates) that undermine or support the documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview a range of relevant witnesses and perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure to interview a range of former National Guardsmen who served with Lieutenant Colonel Killian and who had different perspectives about the documents was cited as a defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek multiple witnesses with different perspectives and direct knowledge; avoid overreliance on a single interviewee whose perspective may be limited or unrepresentative. Disclose limits of firsthand knowledge when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating misleading impressions about what interviewees know
rubrics_metrics.description: The segment conveyed a misleading impression that Lieutenant Strong had authenticated the content of the documents when he did not have the personal knowledge to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit and present interview clips so they do not imply expertise or knowledge the interviewee lacks. Include necessary context and disclaimers when using soundbites that could be misconstrued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a vetting process suited to speed, significance, and sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure to have a vetting process capable of dealing effectively with the production speed, significance, and sensitivity of the segment was a key criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement robust internal vetting procedures that scale to a story's urgency and potential impact; rapid production should not bypass critical checks (authentication, corroboration, conflicts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest and appearances of political coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: A telephone call before the segment's airing by the producer to a senior campaign official of John Kerry was deemed a clear conflict of interest that created the appearance of political bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not coordinate with political campaigns or take actions that could suggest assistance to a campaign. Avoid contacts that create actual or apparent conflicts; disclose any contacts that occur and recuse where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not 'expert-shop'; use the best qualified independent experts
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel criticized efforts to find document examiners who would vouch for authenticity instead of identifying the best examiners available regardless of whether they would support the position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select independent experts based on credentials and reputation, not desired opinions. If multiple expert opinions exist, present the range and reasons for divergence; avoid presenting only supportive views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose expert limitations and avoid misrepresenting expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Some people cited as experts (e.g., defenders found on blogs) lacked appropriate credentials; the analysts originally consulted had expressed reservations that were not fully disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide expert qualifications and transparently report limitations, uncertainties, and the exact scope of their analyses (e.g., signature comparison vs full-document authentication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid having the same personnel defend and produce contested reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing many of the same individuals who produced and vetted the controversial segment to also produce the follow-up news reports defending the segment compounded the damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation of duties: have independent teams review, report, and, if necessary, investigate contested reporting rather than relying on the original producers to mount defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue accurate public statements and avoid overstated claims
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS issued inaccurate press statements asserting the source was 'unimpeachable' and that experts had vouched for authenticity; such inaccurate statements were criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public statements should be conservative and fact-checked; avoid definitive language if evidence is uncertain. Correct the record promptly when inaccuracies are discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare subsequent coverage to investigate criticisms, not to bolster the original segment
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel found that follow-up reporting often sought to support the segment rather than provide accurate and balanced coverage of the controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on disputes over prior coverage, prioritize impartial investigation of the criticisms and new evidence, rather than defending prior narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on poor-quality copies for forensic conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Document examiners noted the evidence was derived from faxed and photocopied duplicates; since CBS used only such copies, authentication to professional standards was impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, obtain original documents for forensic examination; recognize and disclose that low-quality reproductions limit the scope and certainty of forensic conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess typographic and technological anachronisms in documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics focused on anachronisms: proportional spacing, use of Times New Roman, superscripted 'th', and other typography/formatting inconsistent with 1970s typewriter output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forensic review should evaluate fonts, spacing, superscripts, headers, and formatting to determine whether a document's production methods are consistent with the claimed era and technology (typewriter models, typesetting equipment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroborate content details against contemporaneous facts (dates, personnel status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations found substantive inconsistencies (e.g., an officer cited as exerting pressure was discharged before the date of a memo), demonstrating the need to check content against records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify named individuals' positions, service dates, and other factual claims in documents against authoritative records to spot internal inconsistencies that undermine authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious about and disclose intermediary handling that could alter documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Burkett admitted making copies at Kinko's and burning originals; such intermediary actions hindered authentication and raised reliability questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how materials were handled, who made copies, and any alterations or reproductions. If originals have been destroyed or unavailable, disclose that limitation and the implications for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: When errors occur, acknowledge responsibility and remediate
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS News President stated that inability to prove authenticity meant the documents should not have been used and called it a mistake; the network apologized and took personnel actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reporting errors or lapses in standards occur, issue clear acknowledgments, corrections or retractions, and take appropriate internal measures to address process failures and prevent recurrence.
